authenticatedNativeDll.retrieval: Normal authenticated /api/download/lwtool endpoint using the owner's existing saved session. Response was protected with DLLENC1 and was decoded locally using the matching recovered runtime key. Neither session material nor DLL bytes are retained in Git.

facts: Route-C is hard-enabled for current production.
Normal Home reaches _route_c_start_single and returns before the retained older libzstd/folder-swap launch path.
The RouteCSession creates a random BOOT mapping, .key and .mk mappings, .ready and .ack events, a 16-byte nonce and a 32-byte MAC key.
The staged BOOT packet deliberately uses PID 1. Current production does not call Python publish(); the native launcher bridge rebinds the packet to the actual child.
Production checks the server hash for lwtool.dll and downloads the current DLL when absent or mismatched.
RcOrchestrateSingle receives exact official launcher, game executable, game root, DLL path, BOOT name, nonce, random state mapping, instance and timeout fields.
Python waits up to 60 seconds for the Route-C .ack after native orchestration returns.

tooling.method: Targeted PE/Capstone inspection and targeted Ghidra decompilation only; no repeated whole-program analysis.

facts: Creates the official LastWar launcher suspended with a Unicode environment.
Creates a Job Object and assigns the suspended launcher.
Queues RcParentInitialize into the launcher through RcQueueParentBridge.
Resumes the launcher thread only after the parent bridge has been queued.
Waits for Route-C native state to identify and validate the real game child.
Returns the selected child PID through the native result structure.
Failure paths terminate the owned process/job.
Loads the same DLL locally, resolves RcParentInitialize and converts the export to an RVA after validating an x64 PE image.

The active injection helper validates target image/path, allocates two regions in the suspended launcher, writes the loader and data, changes protection, flushes the instruction cache and queues the loader with QueueUserAPC on the launcher thread.
Opens and validates the Route-C state mapping.
Reads the expected game and parent executable identities from Route-C environment values.
Installs interception around kernel32 CreateProcessW/CreateProcessA so the injected launcher bridge observes child creation.
Uses LWINSTANCE as part of the per-instance native identity.
Creates/uses a .relaunch shared state mapping.
Defaults to a 120000 ms native timeout when no timeout is supplied.
Polls at 50 ms inside the native waiter.
Cross-checks process/thread identity with GetProcessIdOfThread.
Requires relevant launcher/game processes to belong to the same Job Object.
Checks executable/process identity, waits on process/state handles, enumerates windows and reads a 0x48-byte state block from the selected game process before accepting the native stage.
Rejects a process that is not on the expected Route-C environment.
Parses LW_ROUTE_C_BOOT_NAME, LW_ROUTE_C_NONCE and LWINSTANCE.
Opens the BOOT and key mappings and validates the LWBIPC1 header, version, size, instance and nonce/key-bound data.
Validates the embedded LuaS v2 payload before publishing it.
Rebinds the staged packet to the real child and signals the ready event.
Queues lwtool.dll into the selected child after the authenticated bind.

nativeRouteC.scopeBoundary: RcOrchestrateMulti contains a separate CreateRemoteThread path. It is feature-gated multi-window behavior and is not attributed to normal single Home.

facts: Each GameClient uses CMD, RESULT and OUT shared-memory mappings of 5 MiB each plus a 16 KiB ERR mapping.
Single production uses the unsuffixed mappings; isolated instances use an instance suffix.
send() serializes calls with a per-client lock and correlates results with callbackId.
Result polling is 3 ms in fast mode; normal calls use 5 ms polling for the first 100 ms then 20 ms.
A normal successful send deliberately sleeps so its total/post-success pacing is at least about 80/30 ms.
Scoped work performs a final live identity check immediately before command bytes are written.
Malformed result JSON with a stable length is retained for up to 0.3 s before being discarded, protecting against reading a partially published result.
Native Route-C .ack proves that the proxy received the BOOT payload; it is not the final application connected state.
The application considers the game connected only after IPC returns a numeric server ID, an authenticated tool session exists and game UID verification succeeds.
If Lua becomes ready after the ordinary boot wait, _late_connect_watch polls every 5 seconds for up to 600 seconds and can promote the same live game to connected without relaunching it.
The automatic reconnect monitor runs on a 5-second cadence.
Sustained IPC failure uses materially longer health windows than a single failed ping; the source distinguishes previously alive IPC from never-alive IPC.
The game watcher waits for three process-missing observations and then cross-checks IPC and memory evidence before declaring a real game death.
Single reconnect clears IPC buffers and re-enters py_start_game with bounded backoff.
Disconnect handling is deduplicated and respects stop/reopen controls.
After launch, generic single health helpers can fall back to image-name-wide LastWar.exe discovery rather than retaining only the native Route-C child identity.
Normal Home Stop executes taskkill /F /IM LastWar.exe /T and therefore targets every matching game image, not the exact Route-C child.
The feature-gated multi-window path maintains per-instance generation and IPC objects.
It can recover exact per-window PIDs from instance environment identity.
Its clean-close path targets the selected instance rather than image-wide LastWar.exe.

lwtoolPerformanceFacts.sharedMemoryReservation: CMD + RESULT + OUT reserve approximately 15 MiB of shared mapping address space per GameClient, plus ERR. Reserved mapping size is not equivalent to resident RAM.
polling: GameClient RESULT polling: 3 ms fast or 5 ms -> 20 ms normal.
Normal successful command pacing has an intentional ~80 ms floor.
UI status refresh: approximately 1 s after the preceding refresh completes.

sourceReportedHistoricalMeasurement.claim: Comments report that, before a 3-second cache was added, repeated multi-window process/window/environment discovery measured roughly 23% of one core with three windows. This is historical source-reported evidence, not a measurement from this research pass.

sourceReportedWorkingSetTrim.claim: The source contains an opt-in low-free-RAM working-set trim. Its comment reports a development observation of game working set 1031 MiB -> 117 MiB immediately -> 225 MiB after 25 s while commit remained 1892 MiB. This changes residency/page-in behavior rather than proving lower committed memory.

observedThisPass: The normal authenticated endpoint returned the protected native DLL with HTTP 200.
The protected DLL header, declared plaintext size, plaintext SHA-256 and MZ PE signature all verified after local decryption.
No LastWar.exe or LastWarLauncher.exe was launched for this research.
No gameplay or account-changing command was performed.
No connected-idle performance benchmark was performed.

revisedVerdict.overall: The earlier blanket statement that LW-Control has the better connection method is no longer supported.
revisedVerdict.launchAttachment: Both are sophisticated. LwTool Route-C uses suspended official-launcher injection and child-process hooks; LW-Control augments the official Lua package before official launch.
revisedVerdict.commandTransport: LwTool has the structurally leaner controller-to-game command path because it uses shared mappings directly, while LW-Control currently has a named-pipe plus Lua/managed file-mailbox boundary. Real latency/CPU superiority is unmeasured.
revisedVerdict.readinessRecovery: Both have substantive readiness and recovery logic. LwTool has strong late-connect recovery; LW-Control has a more explicit exact-session Start readiness contract.
revisedVerdict.singleProcessIsolationAndStop: LW-Control is stronger. It retains PID/path/start/session identity through Stop and restoration. LwTool's normal single Stop is image-wide despite strong native launch identity.
revisedVerdict.efficiency: No winner without an equivalent live benchmark.

remainingGaps: No equivalent command RTT P50/P95 benchmark.
No runtime transport-loss or process-exit recovery timing comparison in this pass.
No live validation of launcher/game update compatibility for either attachment method in this pass.
The exact internal implementation of every CreateProcess hook instruction was not decoded, although the parent hook registration, Route-C bind export and child validation path were recovered.
Actual resident/committed cost of LwTool's 5 MiB mappings is unmeasured.
Feature-gated LwTool multi-window Route-C behavior was not treated as normal Home and was not benchmarked.
